; Descriptor: count byte, then count repetitions of little-endian stream word and register-shadow offset.
; Note bytes below $C0 pack duration class in bits 5..7 and pitch in bits 0..4;
; $C0..$DF carry an extra byte. F2 chooses six duration classes per bank.
; Modulation bytes below $A0 select delay, volume adjustment, pitch/duty or legacy waveform.
; Both grammars share F8 jump, FA call, FB return, FC repeat-count, FD end-repeat and FF stop.
; Flow frames use interpreter RAM, not the CPU stack. The five uncovered FF separators
; are literal noncode bytes; no consumer execution of them is asserted.
; Composite sprite: count followed by count records of Y offset, tile, attributes, X offset.
; The renderer adds signed origin components and clips sprites outside the visible page.
; Classified PRG CPU view: effective physical 8 KiB banks [0,1,2,3].
; Physical offsets include the header; per-instruction islands retain exact encoding.
; iNES header: signature, 2x16 KiB PRG, 4x8 KiB CHR, mapper 1 and horizontal header mirroring. MMC1 runtime control can change mirroring.
; Prepare the intro display: disable NMI around PPUCTRL changes, select sprite patterns, then build the screen.

; When held buttons change, publish them immediately and reset the repeat counter. Otherwise publish at frame twelve, then every six frames through the counter's $80 restart; intervening calls clear player_buttons. This is menu/key-repeat input, separate from controller_pressed.
; Split input A into horizontal/vertical page components, zero both fine scroll bytes and retain the page selectors for the NMI scroll update.
; Wait X frames; X=0 wraps and therefore waits 256. A is preserved by WaitFrame; X counts down.
; Wait X groups of 60 frames while preserving the outer countdown on the stack. NTSC timing makes each group approximately one second.
; Clear bit 7 in both PPUCTRL and its shadow. Other control bits remain intact.
; Shared exit writes A to hardware PPUCTRL and its shadow, then returns.
; Set bit 7 in PPUCTRL through the shared store path; this does not preserve the previous NMI enable state.
; Preserve A. With NMI enabled clear the frame latch and spin until NMI sets it; otherwise poll PPUSTATUS for a fresh vblank edge.
; Serialize five low bits of A, least significant bit first, to the MMC1 control address. A is shifted; mapper register values are not effective 8 KiB bank identities.
; Disable NMI around five serial writes to the low CHR-bank register, then reenable NMI. Input A is the mapper register value, not a physical PRG bank.
; Disable NMI around five serial writes to the high CHR-bank register, then reenable NMI.
; Serialize five bits to the PRG-bank register. Callers must establish valid execution context after a bank change; no universal stable-bank return contract is implied.
; Set the MMC1/mirroring shadow byte to $47. Its upper bits later feed the per-frame MMC1 control value.
; Set mapper control shadow to $4F without writing hardware. Later scroll/control application derives the supported MMC1 mode from it.
; Wait a frame, write zero PPUMASK and clear the queued-video mode flag.
; Input A PPUMASK. Wait for a frame and store it to hardware and video-mode flag; nonzero enables queued transfers.
; Apply the saved PPUMASK and restore scroll plus MMC1 control through the shared display-state routine.
; Fill mode: consume an inline pointer to destination,width,height,value. Reuse the one payload byte for every cell; preserve input A/X/Y through the shared engine.
; Use the existing video_destination instead of a destination in the pointed record. Inline pointer selects width,height and literal bytes. Preserve A/X/Y.
; Literal mode: inline pointer selects destination,width,height,payload. Shared engine skips the inline word on return and preserves A/X/Y.
; Save registers, pop the JSR return address, fetch its two-byte record pointer, and push return+2. Select explicit or precomputed PPU destination, then read two dimensions.
; Read width and height. Width>=height takes row transfers; width<height takes column transfers with PPU increment 32. This is a geometry choice, not a high-bit flag on a dimension.

; For each row choose direct PPU writes when rendering is off or a queued packet otherwise. Literal mode advances the source per byte; fill mode reuses it. Advance destination by 32 and repeat height times.
; Reserve a packet, emit its width and row bytes, then publish the queue write cursor. The consumer runs during NMI.
; Advance PPU destination by one nametable row and continue until the row count expires; restore saved A/X/Y.
; Mark destination high bit as vertical stride. Save the source origin per column; step source by width per row and destination by one per column. Fill mode suppresses source advances.
; Enter the queued column path with PPU increment-32 selection. Append the height and width-strided source bytes, publish the packet, restore the original source and advance to the next column.

; Append the height count, then a column of source bytes. Fill mode reuses one byte; literal/RAM modes advance the source by rectangle width for each row. Publish the complete packet only after all rows are queued; the surrounding loop restores the column origin.
; Advance destination one byte, restore column source origin and advance it once in literal mode, then count down width and restore registers.
; Copy the reader cursor to the writer cursor, making the producer queue empty. This five-byte helper has no known live caller.
; Wait while unsigned write-minus-read occupancy is at least $40. Write destination high/low to the 256-byte ring, retain an unpublished cursor and restore X.
; Append A to the pending packet at its private cursor, preserving X. Publishing is separate so NMI cannot consume an incomplete packet.
; Commit the pending cursor to the queue write position after a complete packet is staged.

; NMI-side consumer. Snapshot the read cursor and process packets until empty or at least $30 bytes have been consumed. Packet format is destination high/low, count, data; destination bit 7 requests PPU increment 32.
; Enforce the byte budget between packets, set PPU address/control, copy the count bytes and publish the read cursor. A palette packet performs the PPU address reset sequence afterward.
; Strobe both standard controllers, then collect eight serial bits per port. Store held state and newly pressed state; the helper falls through once for the second port.
; Read one controller indexed by X, combining the low two serial bits. Shift eight buttons into A; new presses are current AND NOT previous.
; Fill the entire $0200 page with $F0 to hide all sprites and clear stale shadow bytes.
; Save A/X/Y, DMA the $0200 OAM shadow, apply staged PPUMASK, flush video packets and restore scroll/mapper state. Set frame latch, poll input, tick audio and optionally escape to menu.
; When the menu-escape flag and new Start press are both set, clear the flag, reset stack to $FA and jump to MenuEntry. This intentionally abandons the interrupted call chain.
; Normal interrupt exit restores Y, X and A before RTI.
; Reset the PPU address latch/state, derive nametable bits from page selectors, write fine scroll and serialize the control value formed from mapper shadow upper bits plus $1E.
; IRQ vector returns immediately; no classified IRQ service body.
; Initialize APU enables, sentinel/cache state and two output banks. Also writes legacy FDS wave registers; these addresses do not imply FDS support on this MMC1 cartridge.

; Input A effect index; negative stops all effects. Use mask/priority tables to reject lower-priority conflicts, clear conflicting slots, then initialize up to five effect channels from the selected record.
; Resolve an effect record pointer, read its channel count and allocate inactive slots 4..0 with mask/priority metadata.
; OR the five effect-slot channel masks into the hardware-selection mask used by the frame mixer.
; Clear active effect counters/masks, set priorities to $FF and reset the effect register-shadow bank from a 24-byte template.
; 24 initial register-shadow bytes copied to both effect/music channel banks by audio reset.

; Initialize per-slot pitch base, gate, volume/effect state and interpreter-stack cursor. Consume stream pointer low/high and hardware-register offset from the record; decrement the outstanding channel count.
; Store selected music index, clear five music timers and reset its register-shadow bank. A<0 stops; otherwise resolve the sequence record and initialize slots 9..5.
; Each NMI set APU frame-counter mode, run active channels 9..0 through note, gate and modulation interpreters, then mix effect/music register shadows into hardware using the effect channel mask.
; Load each channel output-bank and sequence pointer, tick the note interpreter, save its pointer, handle gate release and run the modulation interpreter with a separate pointer.
; Clear masks of inactive effect slots and rebuild the aggregate mask. For each hardware group choose effect or music shadows, compare the last-written cache and write only changed registers.
; Effect-mask carry selects pulse-1 shadow bank; compare four bytes and write changed APU registers $4000..$4003.
; Repeat bank selection and cache comparison for pulse-2 registers $4004..$4007.
; Copy four selected triangle shadow bytes to $4008..$400B only when changed.
; Copy four selected noise shadow bytes to $400C..$400F only when changed.
; Copy eight selected legacy wave-channel shadow bytes to $4080..$4087 when changed. On this mapper these writes do not establish audible FDS hardware behavior.
; Audio signed-nibble and pitch mode bit masks. Consumer-indexed table; reviewed bounds follow adjacent independent structures and matching producer/reader layouts.
; Decrease the channel event timer; when it expires, consume commands until a timed event or stop. X is channel slot, audio_stream its current pointer and audio_output its shadow-register bank.
; High command bits $E0 route control commands. Otherwise hardware offset distinguishes noise/DMC handling from signed five-bit pitch deltas; $10 denotes a rest.
; Sign-extend the five-bit pitch delta unless it is the rest code, add the channel pitch base and update period registers from the selected period table.
; Obtain event duration and coordinate the gate counter; zero-duration events continue parsing immediately.
; Load duration and set gate to $FF unless a gate ratio is supplied. Repeated addition computes the high byte of duration*ratio. Initialize the selected modulation sequence.
; If modulation selection is nonnegative, use its four-byte descriptor to initialize a modulation pointer and stack cursor, with timer one.
; Top three bits select a duration lookup plus duration-bank offset. Encoded $C0 uses an explicit following byte instead; store the resulting event timer.

; Dispatch note controls: $F0 sets the high volume nibble, $F1 adjusts it with saturation, $F2 selects a six-entry duration bank, $F3 waits, $F4 sets gate ratio, $F5 pitch base and $F6 modulation selection. Other branches update channel pitch/gate and DMC registers before resuming the parser.
; Add a signed stream adjustment to the channel's current high-nibble volume. Clamp overflow to fifteen and underflow to zero, then reuse the shared absolute-volume writer.
; Read one byte, multiply by six and store the duration-table base index.
; Read a direct duration, set gate sentinel $FF and return after advancing the stream.
; Read the next byte as the gate multiplier used for note-duration scaling.
; Read the next byte as the pitch base added to signed note deltas.
; Read the modulation selector. A negative selector enters the alternate descriptor path; continue interpreting commands.
; Store the decoded period-table mode in this channel's audio_period_mode field and resume note parsing. The pitch helper doubles this mode to select a table pointer.
; Write the decoded sample address to DMC address, fetch a second byte for DMC length, then continue parsing. These are APU register mechanics, not a claim that a sample is naturally selected.

; Read the low period byte, preserve the cache's length-control choice while combining the new high nibble, and write the channel's two pitch bytes. Refresh dependent channel state before resuming the parser.
; Read a signed byte and sign-extend into Y before adding it to the selected output period word.
; Store the decoded byte in the shared audio parameter and continue note parsing. Its exact audible effect remains consumer-dependent.
; Byte $FF clears event/modulation timers and silences channel volume. Other values route to shared jump/call/repeat interpretation with the note-stream stack cursor.

; Shared bytecode flow: $F8 jump to inline pointer; $FA call; $FB return; $FC push repeat frame; $FD decrement/repeat/pop. Interpreter frames use a channel-local cursor into shared RAM, separate from the CPU stack.
; For $FA read target pointer and save the continuation as two bytes below the current interpreter stack cursor, then switch streams.
; For $FB restore low/high stream address from the interpreter stack and advance its cursor by two.
; For $FC push saved stream address and repeat count in a three-byte interpreter frame.
; For $FD decrement the frame count. If nonzero reload its stream address; otherwise pop three bytes and advance past the command.
; Increment the 16-bit stream pointer and read at its current Y offset. Many callers enter with Y=0; retain explicit Y semantics.
; Input A pitch index. Select a period-table pointer from channel mode, write its low byte and combine high bits with the toggled length/trigger bit in the output shadow.
; Ignore zero/$FF gates. On countdown expiry select the release descriptor (modulation index*4+2) and initialize its stream.
; Count down modulation timer; when expired decode compact controls. Low command groups set delay, adjust/set volume, or change duty/wave selection; high groups use shared bytecode flow.
; Group zero loads a five-bit delay and advances. Other groups update parameters and continue immediately unless bit 4 requests a one-tick pause.

; Group $20 sign-extends a four-bit period delta and adds it to the selected channel period word. The shared continuation tests bit four to select a one-tick pause versus immediate next-command processing.
; Group $40 sets volume from the low nibble; $60 adds a signed nibble to current volume, saturating to 0..15.

; Group $80 selects pulse duty in the high two output bits. For hardware offset $10 it enables legacy wave RAM writes, copies 64 bytes through the RAM-source pointer and clears the write-enable register. This code does not establish expansion-hardware compatibility.

; High command $F0 reads a byte into the channel's second output register, then continues modulation parsing; $FF stops its timer. Other flow operations reuse the shared interpreter with a separate modulation stack cursor.
; Replace low volume nibble, subtract attenuation from its high nibble and the effect/music master byte, clamp at zero and encode the result for the selected hardware group.
; Choose effect or music master attenuation by slot<5. Convert its high nibble to a subtractive attenuation and clamp the final volume at zero.
; Triangle output is gated on when effective volume is at least four; otherwise write zero.
; Legacy wave volume uses effective volume doubled plus bit 7. Execution of this path does not establish expansion-hardware support.
; Read the command low nibble and sign-extend bit 3 using the mask at $DF6B. Y becomes $FF for a negative nibble, zero otherwise.

; Read the low five bits of the current stream byte without advancing it. Return the sign-extended value in A and the extension byte in Y (zero or $FF), using the fixed bit-four mask. No caller is known.
; Input A low delta and Y high delta. Add this signed word to output registers at hardware offset+2/+3, retaining carry between bytes.
; 75 big-endian pulse periods, decreasing from 2047 to 28. The period consumer reads high then low through the pointer at $E531.
; 72 big-endian increasing words, 64 through 3893. Their frequency-like shape supports noncode data; the exact semantic consumer/scale remains unresolved.
; Sixteen split low waveform-pointer bytes; selectors are masked to four bits. They point into RAM, so this is not evidence of ROM wave images.
; Sixteen matching high waveform-pointer bytes. Legacy wave upload reads 64 RAM bytes through each selected pointer.
; Ten low bytes of output shadow-bank pointers: five effect slots then five music slots. Each channel uses its separate register offset within the selected bank.
; Ten matching high bytes of output shadow-bank pointers, indexed by audio slot. These pair with the low-pointer array at $E509.
; Ten initial note-interpreter stack cursors, one per audio slot.
; Ten initial modulation-interpreter stack cursors; independent of note and CPU stacks.
; Little-endian pointer to the big-endian pulse period table at $E3C3.
; Forty pairs of little-endian modulation pointers: attack/sustain then release.
; 78 duration bytes. F2 parameter times six selects the bank, note classes add 0..5; the inspected stream parameter maximum is twelve, giving final index 77.
; Ten little-endian music descriptor pointers, indexed by selection.
; Twenty-four little-endian effect descriptor pointers; masks and priorities use the same index.
; 24 effect channel masks, indexed with the effect descriptor selection.
; 24 effect priority bytes. All are zero in this ROM; retain as distinct table because the arbiter reads them independently.
; Generic noncode bit patterns between effect priorities and CPU vectors. Repeated FF/00 and masks support data; mapper writes to $FFF9 are hardware writes, not reads of this backing.
; Little-endian NMI/reset/IRQ vector words: $DC88/$C000/$DD04. These are CPU targets in the reset mapping, not physical file offsets.
; 32 KiB CHR backing includes pattern graphics and compressed room byte records.
; Room metadata selects CHR banks 5/6 through PPU reads; this is not exclusively rendered tiles.
; 119 paired-sprite poses. Each four-byte row is tile-left, attribute-left, tile-right, attribute-right.
; AppendSpritePair and DrawPlayerPair place the two sprites eight pixels apart.
; Established mechanical roles. CPU RAM, PPU/APU registers and CPU ROM views are distinct.
; Array aliases name bases, not allocations or immutable ROM identities.
; work_* are shared scratch bytes: their meanings depend on the enclosing routine.
; Table aliases identify CPU views; nearby source comments describe reviewed physical bounds.
; Additional established field and register-cache roles. Scene fields reuse object-array RAM.
; Final self-JMP operand; phases 1/2 read durations, phase 3 reads packet width.
